workingTitle: SPHEREx maps the chemistry of 37 brown dwarf atmospheres
publicationStatus: Peer-reviewed study in The Astrophysical Journal; NASA/JPL public release dated October 8, 2026.
coreFacts: The paper presents 37 high-signal-to-noise SPHEREx spectra spanning brown dwarf classes L0 through Y4, temperatures of about 2,500 to 250 kelvin, and distances of roughly 2 to 30 parsecs.
SPHEREx measured each object from 0.75 to 5 micrometres at resolving power about 40 to 100, covering broad absorption from water, methane, carbon monoxide, and carbon dioxide.

Five modern atmosphere-model grids broadly reproduce the chemical cooling sequence but generally fail to fit the near-infrared peaks and the 4-micrometre window at the same time; the largest disagreements occur around carbon monoxide and carbon dioxide features.

Observed carbon monoxide and carbon dioxide features rise through warmer L and early T dwarfs, then fall sharply as cooler atmospheres become methane dominated, with a marked transition around 1,000 to 700 kelvin.
The authors conclude that model systematics, rather than the observational uncertainty in this curated sample, now limit how confidently physical properties can be inferred.
caveats: The 37-object sample was deliberately curated for high signal-to-noise and subtype coverage, so it is not a population census.
The molecular indices are imperfect because several molecules overlap and no clean continuum exists in these spectra.
At least half of the early observations were subject to under-flagging of bad pixels; the authors masked points more than four standard deviations from a smoothed running median.
Quoted SPHEREx QR2 absolute gain reliability was better than about 3 percent in Bands 1 to 4 and 5 percent in Bands 5 and 6, with calibration still being refined.
sourceStatus: Full primary paper and NASA/JPL release read. The paper is peer reviewed and directly supports the sample, measurements, model comparisons, and caveats; independent secondary corroboration was unnecessary.
